class.name: TiledNavigation3D
class.brief_description: Keeps a navigation mesh in step with a level at runtime, as tiles rebaked when what's in them changes.
class.description: The navmesh is split into square tiles [member tile_size] across, on a grid aligned to the world, each its own navigation region. A tile is rebaked on a worker thread (a low-priority [WorkerThreadPool] task) once what's in it has been quiet for [member bake_delay], or at least every [member max_bake_interval] while it keeps changing, and swapped in on the main thread. Tiles meet edge to edge on a shared cell grid (horizontal and vertical), baked with a border of the agent's radius plus three cells and an edge error of at most 1, so their edges line up; [member use_edge_connections] joins what still doesn't quite. Each tile bakes fixed geometry: [member static_geometry] if set, else whatever [member source_geometry_root] holds, parsed once (with the template's parse settings) and moved into world space. Things that move but stand in the way carve it too: [NavigationObstacle3D] nodes in [member obstacle_group] with [member NavigationObstacle3D.affect_navigation_mesh] enabled. An obstacle's footprint is its vertices, turned and scaled as the node is about Y (as Godot's own obstacle parser projects them), or a circle of its radius scaled by its largest scale axis, round its global position; its prism reaches from the agent's height below it to its height above, so ground a walker would hit it from counts as blocked. An obstacle carves only once it has stayed put for [member obstacle_settle_time]: carving is for what stands still, and something on the move (a driver in a vehicle) is left to avoidance rather than rebaking every tile along its way. When a carving obstacle moves more than a quarter metre or goes away, its tiles are rebaked. With [member NavigationObstacle3D.carve_navigation_mesh] off, the agent's radius is kept clear round it too. A level whose ground the scene tree can't parse (a heightmap terrain) can add it per tile through [method set_tile_geometry_callback]; tiles cover [member area] even where no fixed geometry reaches. Settings (agent size, slope, climb, cells) come from [member template_navigation_mesh]. Its cell size has to divide [member tile_size] into a whole number of cells, or neighbouring tiles won't join up; with [member configure_map] the navigation map's cell size and height are set to match. Agent sizes that aren't whole cells are rounded by the baker, with a warning every bake. Subclasses add geometry that changes by itself; see [VoxelTerrainNavigation].

method.name: bake_all
method.description: Marks every tile for rebaking now, without waiting for [member bake_delay].

method.name: get_navigation_map
method.description: The navigation map the tiles are on: the one given to [method set_navigation_map], else the world's.

method.name: get_pending_tile_count
method.description: Tiles waiting to bake or baking (counting a layout still due as one). Zero once the navmesh matches the level.

method.name: get_statistics
method.description: Tile and bake counts and timings: [code]tiles[/code], [code]pending_tiles[/code], [code]bakes_in_flight[/code], [code]bake_count[/code], [code]bake_usec_last[/code], [code]bake_usec_max[/code], [code]bake_usec_average[/code] (worker time), [code]apply_usec_max[/code] (main thread), [code]dropped_results[/code] (bakes outdated before they finished), [code]obstacles[/code] (carving now), [code]layouts[/code] (times the tiles were laid out, after parsing) and [code]fixed_triangles[/code] (in the fixed geometry at the last layout). Subclasses add their own.

method.name: set_navigation_map
method.description: Puts the tiles on [param map] instead of the world's navigation map.

method.name: set_tile_geometry_callback
method.description: Called on the main thread before each tile bakes, with the tile's baking bounds ([AABB], the tile and its border) and an empty [NavigationMeshSourceGeometryData3D] to add world-space geometry to; it's baked with the tile like the fixed geometry (a subclass's burial test included). Rebakes every tile.

members.member: Tiles cover this box even where no fixed geometry reaches, for ground [method set_tile_geometry_callback] adds. Empty covers only where there's fixed geometry.
Seconds a tile has to go without changes before it is rebaked, so a change made in steps bakes once.
If true, sets the navigation map's cell size and height to the template's.
While false, nothing is baked and the tiles' regions are disabled. Turn it on only where agents path, a multiplayer host for example.
A tile that keeps changing is still rebaked at least this often.
Tile bakes allowed to run at once.
Navigation layers of the tiles' regions.
Seconds an obstacle has to stay put (within a quarter metre) before it carves the navmesh.

Group whose [NavigationObstacle3D] members (with affect_navigation_mesh) carve the navmesh where they stand. They're switched off while [member source_geometry_root] is parsed, so they're never baked in for good.
If true, also bakes while the scene is open in the editor.
Without [member static_geometry], the node whose geometry is parsed (once, when the tiles are laid out) for the fixed geometry. Setting it, even to the same path, parses it again.

Fixed geometry baked into every tile it overlaps, in world space: typically parsed once offline with [method NavigationServer3D.parse_source_geometry_data] and saved, with projected obstructions for props a bake can't see.
Settings every tile bakes with. Its own polygons are not used.
The tiles' regions' edge connections, joining edges of neighbouring tiles that are close but not identical.
Width of a tile, in metres. Smaller tiles rebake less per change; larger ones mean fewer regions.
